name: Graphify
summary: Turns a codebase plus its docs, SQL, configuration files and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph that Claude explores through the /graphify skill; code is parsed locally with tree-sitter.

steps: Confirm you are looking at the canonical project, https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify; forks and mirrors exist.
Install Python 3.10 or newer and uv.
Run `uv tool install graphifyy` (the PyPI package is `graphifyy` with a double y; other graphify* packages are unaffiliated).
install.changes: Adds the `graphify` command to uv's per-user tool environment. Does not touch any project or Claude configuration.

steps: Install Python 3.10 or newer and pipx.
install.changes: Adds the `graphify` command to pipx's per-user tool environment. Does not touch any project or Claude configuration.

steps: In the project root, run `graphify install --project`.
Review the written `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` and the `references/` folder, then commit them to the project repository.
Add `graphify-out/` to the project's .gitignore unless the team wants the graph committed.
install.changes: Writes `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` and a `references/` folder into the current project, visible in Git. The person's Claude configuration is not changed.

steps: Read what the hooks do before enabling them.

`graphify claude install` in a project sets up always-on graph guidance for Claude Code, including hooks that run before Claude's search and file-read tool calls (Grep, Glob, Read); in graphify's strict mode they can deny some of those calls.
`graphify hook install` adds Git hooks that rebuild the graph on commit and checkout.
install.changes: Adds Claude Code configuration and hooks to the project (`graphify claude install`) and Git hooks to the repository (`graphify hook install`). Inspect the changed files with `git status` and `git diff` before committing them.

nexusDelivery: Prefer the project-scoped install (`graphify install --project`) that the person reviews and commits to the project repository, or package the skill as a NEXUS AI Kit and enable it per profile so it reaches sessions through a session-scoped plugin directory. NEXUS never runs `graphify install` itself and never registers the skill in a Claude configuration directory.
dataFlow: Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter and stays on the machine. Docs, PDFs and images are sent to the assistant's model or a configured backend for extraction; `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none` or the `--code-only` option keeps the graph code-only, and `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=ollama` keeps everything local. Query calls are logged to `~/.cache/graphify-queries.log` unless `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_DISABLE=1` is set. The project states that it collects no telemetry.
security: Install only the PyPI package `graphifyy` and check the project at https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify; similarly named packages, forks and mirrors are unaffiliated.
Do not run `graphify install` without `--project`: it registers the skill in the person's assistant profile, which changes their Claude configuration outside NEXUS profile isolation.
Review `graphify claude install` before enabling it: its hooks run before Claude's search and file-read calls in the project and, in strict mode, can deny some of them.
If organisation-managed Claude Code settings restrict hooks, skills or plugins, they win; do not work around them.
Review the Git hooks added by `graphify hook install` like any other hook; they run on every commit and checkout.
For employer or client code whose docs must not leave the machine, set `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=ollama` or use code-only mode (`GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none` or `--code-only`) before graphing docs, PDFs or images.
The query log records the questions asked; set `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_DISABLE=1` when questions may contain confidential details.
`graphify-out/` can contain content extracted from docs; keep it in .gitignore unless the team has decided to commit it.
usage: `/graphify .` builds the graph for the current project.
`/graphify ./docs --update` updates the graph for the docs folder after changes.
`/graphify query "<question>"` answers a question from the graph.
`/graphify path "A" "B"` shows how two components or concepts are connected.
`/graphify explain "X"` explains one node and its relationships.
Outputs land in `graphify-out/`: graph.html (interactive view), GRAPH_REPORT.md (report) and graph.json (machine-readable graph).
Uninstall with `graphify uninstall` (`--purge` also deletes graphify-out/); `graphify claude uninstall` removes the project's Claude Code hooks.
